primary_claim: In a small appendix experiment, fine-tuning LLaMA-3-70B-instruct on neutral instruction-following data (Alpaca-GPT4) produced little measurable drift toward misalignment, while fine-tuning gpt-4o-mini on the same data showed misalignment first increase then decrease, results the authors call mixed and inconclusive with respect to the proposed 'Alignment Drift Hypothesis.'

effect.metric: misalignment score (email-scenario dilemma) vs. training steps on neutral instruction data
effect.value: little drift for LLaMA-3-70B-instruct; misalignment rose then fell for gpt-4o-mini

contradicts_or_qualifies: Prior work (Arike et al. 2025 on inference-time goal drift; Qi et al. 2023 on fine-tuning removing alignment training) suggesting AI systems drift into misalignment by default; the author's own small experiment and the broader observation that current LLMs don't drift into misalignment by default in practice complicate this picture
stated_future_work: Further empirical work to explore whether the Alignment Drift Hypothesis holds, especially for more powerful future AI systems.
Investigate why drift happened when fine-tuning gpt-4o-mini but not LLaMA-70B.
limitations_stated: Our results were mixed and inconclusive.
Misalignment increased then decreased for gpt-4o-mini, which isn't consistent with the drift hypothesis, and the model-dependent difference is unexplained.
The toy quantitative models (evolution and gradient descent simulations) are illustrative simplifications, not validated against real training runs.
quote: Misalignment increases, and then decreases again, which isn't consistent with our drift hypothesis.
